firstPlayerRule: The player who most recently set foot on an island takes the first action turn.
houseFallback: If the criterion leaves a tie, nobody qualifies, or your group prefers another approach, agree to choose randomly. This is this site’s suggested fallback.
clarifications: Give that player the Chieftain Marker. Initial boat placement starts with their right-hand neighbor and runs counterclockwise, ending with the starter.
After card drafting, the Chieftain Marker holder begins the action phase, followed by clockwise turns.
For the next era, the player with the most Island Runes receives the marker. If tied, it goes to the tied player who acted latest in the previous era's order.
Solo play is different: you take the first action turn in every era, before the Enemy Clan.

internalEvidence: Read all 9 cached rule sections in full, including setup, turn sequence and relevant variants. Dized identifies Gamelyn Games as publisher and labels these rules publisher-maintained. Setup step 7 assigns the Chieftain by island recency; step 8 uses reverse initial boat placement. Phase 1 drafts cards before Phase 2's explicit sequential action turns. Cleanup's Rune tie-break only determines later eras and is not an initial-start tie-break. Two-player setup changes do not replace the initial criterion; Solo Player Setup and Solo Action Changes explicitly give the human the first action each era. Credits state copyright 2022.
